title: feat(status-pages): JSON view and atomic JSON apply for the editor, API and MCP

summaries.body:
## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 10/10** · safe to merge Destructive whole-page replace is pinned by PGlite service tests, endpoint tests and MCP tool tests; only the change summaries are computed from the wrong document. 2 notes · tests covered · risk medium · 3/3 new units observable Adds a whole-page JSON config document: `GET`/`PUT /v2/status_pages/{id}/config`, one service write that replaces the page and its components, MCP get/apply tools and a web JSON tab. The write path is sound and well tested; the change summaries read the payload instead of what was written. - `StatusPageConfig` document and `diffStatusPageConfig` in `@maple/domain/http/v2` - `StatusPagesService.applyConfig` replaces page and components in one transaction - New `GET`/`PUT /v2/status_pages/{id}/config` v2 endpoints, write gated on admin - Web JSON tab plus MCP `get_status_page_config`/`apply_status_page_config` tools ### Findings
🔵 Note · F1 · Audit counts diff the request payload, not the applied document correctness · [`apps/api/src/routes/v2/status-pages.http.ts:357`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/12f52714d6f3ac11b502fe529177f613d319bc2f/apps/api/src/routes/v2/status-pages.http.ts#L357) `diffStatusPageConfig` runs against `payload`, so the normalization `selectComponents` applies during the write is counted as a change: a component with `"name": " API "` whose row the service leaves untouched still lands in `changes.components.updated`, and the audit record reports `components_updated: 1` for a no-op. `applied` is already in scope and is what the service actually wrote, so diff that instead. `apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/status-pages.ts:653` repeats this with `params.config`, so the model's "Components updated" list can name a component nothing changed on. ``` const changes = diffChangeSet(diffStatusPageConfig(previous, applied)); ```
🔵 Note · F2 · apply_status_page_config diffs the payload, not the applied config correctness · [`apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/status-pages.ts:653`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/12f52714d6f3ac11b502fe529177f613d319bc2f/apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/status-pages.ts#L653) The diff compares `before` to `params.config`, the request payload, instead of `config`, the document `applyConfig` actually wrote. Because `selectComponents` trims names, descriptions and groups before storing them, an unchanged component re-sent as `"name": " API "` lands in `updated`, so the model reports "Components updated: API" and loses the "Nothing changed" notice for a request that changed nothing. ``` const { fields, created, updated, deleted, reordered } = diffStatusPageConfig(before, config) ```
### Production impact
Telemetry this change adds and removes (6) - ➕ span name `McpTool.getStatusPageConfig` · `apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/status-pages.ts:600` - ➕ span name `McpTool.applyStatusPageConfig` · `apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/status-pages.ts:634` - ➕ span name `StatusPagesService.getConfig` · `packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPagesService.ts:1310` - ➕ span name `StatusPagesService.applyConfig` · `packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPagesService.ts:1323` - ➕ attribute `maple.status_page.actor` · `packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPagesService.ts:1332` - ➕ attribute `maple.status_page.config_components` · `packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPagesService.ts:1333`
What was checked - Order and ids survive a round trip: ids decode via `fromPublicId`, kept components are re-ordered by index (`StatusPagesService.ts:874`) - `StatusPageConfigTheme` covers every `StatusPageTheme` field, so applying cannot silently drop a theme setting - `applyConfig` refuses ids from another page and duplicate ids, and every component exists after the transaction commits

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 10/10** · safe to merge Atomic apply, page locking, the `if_version` conflict and the 200-component cap are pinned by service, route and MCP tests; only the JSON error scanner's unbounded recursion is unprotected. 1 note · tests covered · risk medium · 4/4 new units observable Adds a whole-page config document with an atomic, admin-only apply across API v2, MCP and a new editor JSON tab. The earlier audit/diff findings are fixed at this head and the write path is locked and preconditional; safe to merge. - `applyConfig` replaces a page in one transaction under a `FOR UPDATE` page lock with one bump - `PUT /v2/status_pages/{id}/config` applies with an `if_version` content-version precondition, 409 on conflict - MCP `get_status_page_config` and destructive `apply_status_page_config`, admin-only, unknown keys refused - Editor JSON tab validates drafts live and applies through a single PUT ### Findings
🔵 Note · F3 · scanMembers recurses unbounded, so a deeply nested draft throws instead of reporting a syntax error correctness · [`apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/config-json.ts:68-71`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/55605973d472187eaf142cd1833c777f360c10ab/apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/config-json.ts#L68-L71) `scanMembers` → `scanValue` → `scanMembers` has no depth bound, and it only runs after `JSON.parse` has already failed, on unchecked pasted text. A draft such as `"[".repeat(20000)` overflows the JS stack inside `syntaxProblem`, and the `RangeError` escapes `parseDraft` (`draftOf` is called from `editView` and `canApply`) instead of producing the `Syntax` problem the tab is built to show. ``` Thread a depth counter through `scanValue`/`scanMembers`/`scanProperty` and return `fail(at, "Nested too deeply")` past a small limit (a few hundred), so the tab always shows a problem rather than throwing. ```

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 8/10** · likely safe to merge The atomic replace is locked and well tested; the one gap is the editor sending a freshly re-read `if_version` for a draft built from an older read. 1 warning −1 · tests covered · risk high −1 · 3/3 new units observable Adds a status-page config document with a one-transaction `PUT …/config` apply, two MCP tools and an editor JSON tab, all sharing one diff. The replace semantics hold; the editor defeats its own `if_version` guard. The open `McpQueryError`s at `registry.ts` are warehouse query failures this diff does not touch. - `StatusPagesService.applyConfig` replaces page, theme and components in one locked transaction with a single bump - `GET`/`PUT /v2/status_pages/{id}/config` with an `if_version` precondition and unknown keys rejected - MCP `get_status_page_config` and admin-only, destructive `apply_status_page_config` - Editor gains a JSON tab with a draft scanner, change summary and Apply ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F4 · applyJson sends the newest read's version, not the draft's base version correctness · [`apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/update-json.ts:79`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/322963918f66cb7341ae16be84e6e2d49a06c64e/apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/update-json.ts#L79) The draft is built from the config read at `editJson`, but the `if_version` precondition is taken from `currentConfigOf(model)` at apply time, and `routeChanged` re-reads the config (`readConfig(context, "Refresh")`, `update.ts:148`) whenever the JSON tab is re-entered or another tab saves a component, while `jsonDraft` survives (`jsonDraft` is only cleared by Cancel, a successful apply and `init`). A draft made before that refresh therefore applies under the fresh version, so the server's conflict check cannot fire and a component added in between is deleted, exactly the loss `if_version` exists to prevent. ``` Record the config version alongside the draft (in `editJson`: `jsonDraftVersion: current.version`) and pass that as `ifVersion`, so a refresh of `model.config` cannot launder a stale draft; a conflict then lands in `appliedJson`'s existing `status_page_conflict` path, which re-reads the config. ```
### Fixed since the last review - ✅ ~~F3 · `scanMembers` recurses unbounded, so a deeply nested draft throws instead of reporting a syntax error~~ ### Production impact

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 8/10** · likely safe to merge F4's base-version fix is correct and pinned by a new scene test; one dead-end remains in the editor's conflict path. 1 warning −1 · tests covered · risk medium · 2/3 new units observable −1 The JSON tab now keeps the config document a draft was opened from, so Apply sends that document's `version` and a mid-edit re-read can no longer hide someone else's change (F4 fixed). One dead-end remains: after a conflict the retained draft can never be applied. Safe to merge once that is closed. The open `McpQueryError` issues from `registry.ts` are untouched — that diff only adds `parseOptions` for unknown-key rejection. - `editJson` records `jsonBase`, and `draftOf` parses and diffs drafts against it - `applyJson` sends `jsonBase.version` as `ifVersion`, not the newest read's - `routeChanged` re-reads the config only while the JSON tab is open ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F5 · After a status_page_conflict the draft can never be applied correctness · [`apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/update-json.ts:150-151`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/74c6c0178757f0320306f6d6cd4b4f91eee69f48/apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/update-json.ts#L150-L151) `appliedJson` keeps `jsonDraft` and the stale `jsonBase` on a conflict, so the next Apply sends the same `ifVersion` and the server refuses it again, forever. `canApply` never looks at `jsonFailure`, so the Apply button stays enabled next to the "The page's config changed since it was read." alert, and the only exit (`Reset` or `Cancel` then `Edit`) throws the typed draft away. Block Apply while the last failure was a conflict, or rebase `jsonBase` onto the re-read config so a second Apply sends the new version. ``` Add `model.jsonFailure?.code !== "status_page_conflict" &&` to `canApply` (update-json.ts:48), or set `jsonBase` from the re-read config when the failure was a conflict. ```

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 8/10** · likely safe to merge Held at 8 because a warning is open. 1 warning −1 · 1 note · tests covered · risk medium · 1/1 new units observable The patch adds a JSON view/editor tab that reads `GET /config` and applies a whole `StatusPageConfig` document in one atomic write, exposed through API v2 and MCP tools. Validation, 409-conflict handling and tenant scoping look sound. - New `GET`/`PUT /v2/status_pages/{id}/config` document endpoints with `if_version` optimistic concurrency - `applyConfig` replaces settings, theme and components atomically with one revision bump - New MCP tools `get_status_page_config` and `apply_status_page_config` - Editor gains a JSON tab with validation, change summary and atomic apply ### Findings
🔵 Note · F6 · cancelJson leaves isRebasingJson set, so a later draft is rebased onto the next config read correctness · [`apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/update-json.ts:76`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/20d55e4a6b48ade87f2232e799d54757d4d97a85/apps/web/src/page/alerts/status-pages/editor/update-json.ts#L76) A conflict sets `isRebasingJson` and only `rebaseJsonDraft` clears it, and only while a draft exists (`update-json.ts:162-168`). Cancel while that re-read is in flight (the button is enabled, `isApplyingJson` is already false) or after it failed, then open a new draft: the flag is still set, so the next config read — a tab switch away and back re-reads it — replaces that draft's `jsonBase` mid-edit. The Apply then sends the newer version instead of conflicting, and the summary describes the other admin's change as part of this apply. ``` : { model: { ...model, jsonDraft: null, jsonBase: null, isRebasingJson: false, jsonFailure: null } } ```

<sub>`5379427` · Updated on every push. Reply "won't fix" to dismiss a finding, or mention @maple-review-bot to ask about one.</sub>

inline.body:
> [!WARNING]
> **`applyJson` sends the newest read's version, not the draft's base version**
>
> <sub>F4 · Warning · correctness</sub>

The draft is built from the config read at `editJson`, but the `if_version` precondition is taken from `currentConfigOf(model)` at apply time, and `routeChanged` re-reads the config (`readConfig(context, "Refresh")`, `update.ts:148`) whenever the JSON tab is re-entered or another tab saves a component, while `jsonDraft` survives (`jsonDraft` is only cleared by Cancel, a successful apply and `init`). A draft made before that refresh therefore applies under the fresh version, so the server's conflict check cannot fire and a component added in between is deleted, exactly the loss `if_version` exists to prevent.

```
Record the config version alongside the draft (in `editJson`: `jsonDraftVersion: current.version`) and pass that as `ifVersion`, so a refresh of `model.config` cannot launder a stale draft; a conflict then lands in `appliedJson`'s existing `status_page_conflict` path, which re-reads the config.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **After a `status_page_conflict` the draft can never be applied**
>
> <sub>F5 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`appliedJson` keeps `jsonDraft` and the stale `jsonBase` on a conflict, so the next Apply sends the same `ifVersion` and the server refuses it again, forever. `canApply` never looks at `jsonFailure`, so the Apply button stays enabled next to the "The page's config changed since it was read." alert, and the only exit (`Reset` or `Cancel` then `Edit`) throws the typed draft away. Block Apply while the last failure was a conflict, or rebase `jsonBase` onto the re-read config so a second Apply sends the new version.

```
Add `model.jsonFailure?.code !== "status_page_conflict" &&` to `canApply` (update-json.ts:48), or set `jsonBase` from the re-read config when the failure was a conflict.
```
